This page is generated from `hearthwork <command> --help`, so it always matches the installed version. Run `hearthwork --help` for the short list.

## claude, codex, opencode, aider, qwen

Each agent launcher passes every argument after its name to the agent itself, so `--help` there shows the agent's own help. Hearthwork's own flag is `--dry-run`, and only as the first argument.

```text
hearthwork <claude|codex|opencode|aider|qwen> [--dry-run] [agent arguments]
```

## agents

```text
hearthwork agents             supported agents: installed?, version, API, how Hearthwork connects each
```

## task

```text
usage: hearthwork task [-h] [--agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}] [--allow PATTERN]
                       [--cwd CWD] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--json] [--dry-run]
                       task

Run one coding task with the local model through a coding agent.

positional arguments:
  task                  what to do; "-" reads it from stdin

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}
  --allow PATTERN       command pattern the agent may run, e.g. "pytest *" (not Codex or Aider;
                        repeatable)
  --cwd CWD             folder to work in (default: here)
  --timeout TIMEOUT     seconds before the agent is killed (default 900)
  --json                report as JSON
  --dry-run             print the command, environment and generated files; start nothing
```

## start

```text
usage: hearthwork start [-h] [--model MODEL] [--context CONTEXT] [--force] [--over-budget]

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL      part of a model file name; skips the model menu
  --context CONTEXT  context for this start, e.g. 98304 or 96K (default: auto, see `hearthwork
                     context`)
  --force            interrupt running requests
  --over-budget      start even if the memory estimate exceeds the budget
```

## logs

```text
usage: hearthwork logs [-h] [--server] [-f] [-n N]

Show the host's log (requests, queue, start and stop).

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --server      show llama-server's own output instead
  -f, --follow  keep printing new lines (Ctrl+C stops)
  -n N          how many lines to start with (default 100)
```

## diagnose

```text
usage: hearthwork diagnose [-h] [--last N] [--since DURATION] [--all] [--client CLIENT] [--json]
                           [--export FILE]

Explain what limited your agent sessions, from measured requests (HOME/logs/requests.jsonl).
Nothing leaves this computer; prompts and code are not recorded.

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --last N          only the last N requests
  --since DURATION  only requests from the last period, e.g. 90s, 30m, 2h, 1d
  --all             every recorded request, not only the last 24 hours (the default)
  --client CLIENT   only this client (part of its id, e.g. opencode, api, share)
  --json            print the report as JSON
  --export FILE     write a sanitized JSON report (numbers only: no prompts, code, or credentials)
```

## status

```text

```

## share

```text
usage: hearthwork share [-h] [--port PORT] [--allow-public] [--tailscale]

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit
  --port PORT
  --allow-public  share even on a network Windows calls Public
  --tailscale     accept only Tailscale computers (and this local network when it is not Public):
                  safe on any Wi-Fi
```

## api

```text
usage: hearthwork api [-h] [--port PORT] [--api-key API_KEY] [--allow-switch] [--show]

One local OpenAI + Anthropic compatible endpoint for the running model (Ctrl+C stops it). It
listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1); to use the model from other devices run `hearthwork
share`.

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --port PORT        port to listen on (default 8080)
  --api-key API_KEY  require this key (Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key); without it any program
                     on this computer may use the model
  --allow-switch     a request whose "model" is part of another local model file name restarts the
                     server with it (interrupts everyone using the model); otherwise any model
                     name uses the running model
  --show             print copy-paste setup for the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, curl, Aider, OpenCode,
                     Continue, Cursor and exit
```

## connect

```text
usage: hearthwork connect [-h] [--pin PIN] [--name NAME] [host]

positional arguments:
  host         host or host:port (default: look on the local network)

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --pin PIN    the PIN shown on the host (otherwise asked)
  --name NAME  name for this device on the host (default: this computer's name)
```

## bench

```text
usage: hearthwork bench [-h] [--agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}] [--all] [--warmup]
                        [--show]

Benchmark the running model through a coding agent.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}
  --all                 release check: every installed agent, one after another, after a warmup
  --warmup              run the 30K-token warmup even for a single agent (--all always does)
  --show                only print the scoreboard
```

## tune

```text
usage: hearthwork tune [-h] [--time TIME] [--min-context N]
                       [--agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}] [--quick-tasks N] [--dry-run]
                       [--json]

Try a few installed configurations and save the best tested one as a profile (nothing is
downloaded; the original model is restored).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --time TIME           time limit for the whole run, e.g. 30m, 90s or 1h (default 30m)
  --min-context N       minimum context a candidate must offer, e.g. 65536 or 64K
  --agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}
                        agent to drive the tasks
  --quick-tasks N       how many of the graded tasks to run per candidate (default 3)
  --dry-run             list the candidates and their estimated needs, then exit
  --json                print the result as JSON
```

## doctor

```text
usage: hearthwork doctor [-h] [--agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}] [--all] [--quick]
                         [--json] [--keep]

Check that the model server, the relay and your coding agents work together.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --agent {aider,claude,codex,opencode,qwen}
                        check one agent (default: every installed agent)
  --all                 every installed agent (the default)
  --quick               skip the coding task
  --json                print the report as JSON
  --keep                keep the temporary folders
```

## setup

```text
usage: hearthwork setup [-h] [--update-llama] [--reset] [--import FOLDER]

Set up llama.cpp for Claude Code on this computer.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --update-llama   download the newest llama.cpp build
  --reset          ask for the models folder again
  --import FOLDER  copy settings, llama.cpp and caches from an older Hearthwork folder (a git
                   clone)
```
